framing: Unanimous and the strongest single signal in TREE: none of the thirteen adopts another organisation's taxonomy as its own. Where two taxonomies meet, every observed mechanism is a mapping or a dual tree, never a replacement — but that precedent rests on two cells (n = 2 of 14 rows, 5 not collected). The 0-of-13 is evidence about what platforms do; only Tokopedia Era B is evidence about what a seller facing two trees does. Our numbers: the taxonomy has no node for instant noodles, none for Batik / Mukena / Sajadah / Sambal / Terasi (~2,800 products), no net-content attribute; 25.7 % of our used nodes (32.7 % of products) map mechanically and 28.6 % of those map wrong (Wilson CI 14–50 %); 302 nodes (40 % of products) carry a gender/age level the taxonomy models as an attribute.

rows.shape: “❗ Not creatable” — 12 patterns over 877 doc files / 16,441,164 B → 0 hits each; additions announced via PRODUCT_TYPE_DEFINITIONS_CHANGE.NewProductTypes. Inference: a closed registry is how 107 food types stay 107. Mapping: not collected.

rows.h: it IS the standard; mapping is the point
rows.shape: Centrally authored, open-source. The same release ships 14,528 Shopify→Google mapping rules plus four version-migration sets (5,595 from 2022-02, 108 from 2025-12, 50 from 2024-10, 1 from 2025-09). README (md5 5d197d41…): “🌍 Global Standard: … a universal language for product classification”; “👩🏼‍💻 Integration Friendly: … designed for effortless integration into any system”; audiences split “Integrators: … You want stable distribution files” vs “Taxonomists: Those who want to evolve the taxonomy itself”; “🗺️ Mapping to other taxonomies … rules that can be used to convert between categories and attributes in the Shopify taxonomy to … another taxonomy.” — the vendor describing option (c). Whether a third party may extend locally and stay compatible: not collected (docs/ outside the sparse checkout).
